# Platform reference

Every class in `assets/scripts/platform/`, from its doc comments. The overview is in [README.md](README.md).

- [RunEnvironment](#runenvironment)

## RunEnvironment

`res://assets/scripts/platform/RunEnvironment.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

Facts about where this run of the game is, asked in one place. So far: whether it has a display.

Use:

```gdscript
if RunEnvironment.is_headless(): ...        # nothing is drawn: a test, or a dedicated server (Godot started with --headless)
if not RunEnvironment.runs_visuals(): ...   # a visual-only part (a toy figure, a floating sword) has nothing to do
```

A test that checks visual parts while running headless turns `visuals_without_display` on.

### Settings and properties

- `visuals_without_display: bool` = `false`: On: visual-only parts run even with no display. Off (the default): with no display they build nothing and never run, since nothing can see them (the floating swords cost 1.4 ms a tick on a headless mass battle server).

### Functions

- `is_headless() -> bool` *(static)*: True when nothing is drawn: Godot was started headless, as tests and dedicated servers are.
- `runs_visuals() -> bool` *(static)*: True if visual-only parts should run: there's a display, or visuals_without_display is on.

## ScriptOverrides

`res://assets/scripts/platform/ScriptOverrides.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

Whether a script overrides a function of the script it extends: one place for a question several systems ask.

The AbilityManager asks it to run only the abilities that have an every_tick() of their own, and which actions' readiness follows the body (can_start()); a behaviour, whether the C++ decider can judge it (is_available(), score()); the target selector, whether a game scores targets its own way (target_priority()). The answer is worked out once per script and function, and kept. It counts the entries of that name in the script's method list, which includes the scripts it extends: two or more means an override.

```gdscript
ScriptOverrides.overrides(ability.get_script(), &"every_tick")   # true for Dash, false for Walk
```

### Functions

- `overrides(script: Script, function_name: StringName) -> bool` *(static)*: True if script, or a script between it and its base, overrides function_name. False for a null script, or a function only the base defines.
